articles.author: Miles Parks
articles.description: Election officials in Los Angeles County say their preliminary analysis of the federal government's list of 20,000 "likely" noncitizens registered to vote in California shows the list is "unreliable."
articles.title: Some on DOJ's 20,000 "likely" noncitizen list in Calif. appear to be U.S.-born

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Nigeria is the latest country to report an Ebola case as the outbreak spreads across the region. Kenya confirmed its first case earlier this month and has since recorded nine infections.
articles.title: Nigeria confirms an Ebola case in Abuja as a woman arriving from Uganda tests positive

articles.author: Diane Cole
articles.description: A respected figure in the world of global health, Dr. Kerry takes on a new responsibility. She says it's challenging but not "daunting."
articles.title: Vanessa Kerry is the new WHO envoy for health resilience. What's on her to-do list?

articles.author: Heller McAlpin
articles.description: It is hard not to fall in love with Katherine Browne, the eager to please, mini-skirted narrator in Barbara Trapido's 40-plus-year-old debut novel, reissued this month.
articles.title: 'Brother of the More Famous Jack' finds its way to a new generation of readers

articles.author: Greg Rosalsky
articles.description: Research on past recessions suggests downturns can accelerate automation. That raises the specter of a double whammy for workers.
articles.title: What if an AI bubble bursts — and that accelerates AI job losses?

articles.author: Dabin Han
articles.description: Comic artist Dabin Han shares how backpacking as a novice has helped her push through discomfort and allowed her to make new friends across the country.
articles.title: COMIC: Backpacking teaches artist lessons in patience, trust and friendship

articles.author: Joe Hernandez
articles.description: Here's what's behind the fluctuating costs of everyday grocery items such as ground beef, eggs and chocolate chip cookies.
articles.title: Why these 5 everyday items fluctuate in price at the grocery store

articles.author: Cory Turner
articles.description: The new scholarship tax credit program could help public school families pay for some educational services, but advocates worry it could do more harm than good.
articles.title: Can the new federal voucher program help public schools? Democrats are torn

articles.author: Katie McQue
articles.description: The warnings surfaced in a trove of unreported court records. "I have been fighting about fixing this for months with people who didn't think the harms are severe enough," wrote one executive.
articles.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The Rays will face the NL champion Milwaukee Brewers in the first matchup in which both teams are seeking their first World Series title since 1980.
articles.title: Rays will face Brewers in World Series to produce a first-time champion

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Friend of accused double murderer tells supreme court that van had lemony smell and blue tarp in back before Bunnings stop
Beau Lamarre-Condon played Taylor Swift’s song No Body, No Crime while attempting to dispose of two corpses, a court has heard.
The NSW supreme court has been told he was driving to Bungonia with a friend when the song was played in the van.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly played Taylor Swift’s No Body, No Crime during body disposal, court told

articles.author: Julian Borger in Belgrade
articles.description:
Unorthodox campaign is challenging the ruling party’s 12-year reign with a bold democratic experiment
On a cool autumn evening, a team of Serbian student volunteers went canvassing in the housing estates of Krnjača, a Belgrade suburb. They were equipped with lanyards emblazoned with the word “victory”, a stock list of questions and a mobile app that mapped visited homes and the level of support in each.
The volunteers were part of a mass student movement, Student List, that has rocked Serbia with two years of constant protests. On Sunday, the group will represent the most serious challenge Aleksandar Vučić has faced in his 12 increasingly authoritarian years in power, by putting forward their own candidates in parliamentary elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A student protest movement has gripped Serbia for two years. This weekend it will try to take power

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo and Quique Kierszenbaum in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Rights groups say the planned 1.4km route, which ends at compound run by far-right settler group Elad, will displace Palestinians and reshape the cultural landscape

A fifth foreign company has pulled out of a plan to build a cable car from West to East Jerusalem that threatens to involve the seizure of land and property rights from dozens of Palestinian families along its route, but local authorities insist the scheme is proceeding as planned.
The project appeared to have stalled for four years until late September, just weeks before Israel’s 27 October elections, when the Jerusalem Development Authority (JDA) issued a notice of intent to award a contract without a public tender to ROPES, a cable car engineering consultancy based in South Tyrol, Italy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fifth foreign firm pulls out of controversial Israeli cable car project to East Jerusalem

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
During a summer fire that destroyed homes in Stourbridge, low pressure meant filling a water carrier took 40 minutes
Concerns have been raised about how drought affects the UK’s ability to cope with wildfires after MPs were told firefighters struggled for water supplies during this year’s record summer.
The government has been urged to set out water companies’ statutory responsibilities during major fire incidents to improve the country’s preparedness for the years ahead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Firefighters voice growing concerns over water supplies to tackle UK wildfires

articles.author: Adeshola Ore
articles.description:
Independent MP’s condition remains critical on Wednesday after surgery to save her remaining leg

‘Deeply appalled’: politicians condemn alleged attack after Helen Haines critically injured

Helen Haines, the principled MP respected across parliament

Anthony Albanese has described the police interview on Tuesday with Brendan Nugent as “extensive” but that the motivation of the alleged “violent” attack against Helen Haines is still unknown.
Certainly, it’s a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago.
But I think that Australians do want to see their politicians be able to go about their business, to be able to get something from the back of their car, for goodness sake.
My side, every side included. We all have to recognise that politics has got more aggressive.
The particular impact on women in politics … [They] have got a different form of vilification and aggression towards them as well.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police charge accused Brendan Nugent with additional offences – as it happened

articles.author: Catie McLeod
articles.description:
Ghanda and Windsor Smith are among lowest-rated in Baptist World Aid ethical fashion report based on metrics such as wages and sustainability

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Online fast-fashion giant Shein is outperforming many Australian high street retailers on ethical standards, according to an industry review.
The 11th Baptist World Aid ethical fashion report, released on Tuesday, assessed the ethical practices of 138 Australian and international companies, representing 543 fashion brands.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fast-fashion giant Shein outperforms several Australian retailers on ethics, report says

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy, Henry Belot and Benita Kolovos
articles.description:
AFP commissioner says MPs are generally concerned about growing volume of abuse and intimidation

Follow our live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The head of the Australian federal police has condemned a “febrile” political environment that has seen one person charged every week over the alleged threatening of MPs, as Victoria announces new steps to protect politicians.
But the AFP and Victoria police insist they had no intelligence to suggest 43-year-old Brendan Nugent would go on to allegedly drive a Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP Helen Haines in a targeted attack.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Student told the university’s police department that assault by two men occurred in August during a night of drinking
A sorority member at the University of Arizona has alleged she was sexually assaulted by two men at a fraternity house during a night of drinking in late August.
The student told the university’s police department that she consensually kissed one of the men at one point while at the Sigma Phi Epsilon house on 26 August but doesn’t remember agreeing to sex, according to search warrant records posted Monday night by KOLD-TV in Tucson.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: University of Arizona sorority member alleges sexual assault at fraternity house

articles.author: Dani Anguiano, Uwa Ede-Osifo, Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat and Maya Yang (earlier)
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

A new survey reveals a widening “empathy gap” between Republicans and white evangelicals and the rest of the American public.
On Tuesday, the nonpartisan Public Religion Research Institute released its annual American Values Survey. The survey found that white evangelical Protestants are the only religious group in which a majority does not agree that empathy is foundational moral value (42%). Instead, a majority (54%) say empathy can be dangerous when it leads people away from a society guided by God’s truth, PRRI said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he will have spent $400m to support Republicans in midterms – as it happened

articles.author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
articles.description:
Andrew Hauser says central bank faces ‘hard choices’ as it looks to balance risks of entrenched inflation with desire to protect labour market

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The chance of a fifth interest rate hike on Melbourne Cup day has jumped after Andrew Hauser, the Reserve Bank’s deputy governor, warned of “hard choices” amid a “materially worse” inflation outlook.
Hauser, speaking at an investment bank conference in Sydney on Wednesday morning, said the RBA monetary policy board members were juggling a slowing economy with fears that Australians were starting to lose faith in the central bank’s ability to bring inflation back to the 2.5% target.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Odds of fifth interest rate hike this year shorten as RBA deputy warns inflation outlook ‘worsening’

articles.author: Sian Cain
articles.description:
Morgan Carey sued his sister over claims in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey, which he said falsely portrayed him as a violent drug dealer
A judge has dismissed a lawsuit from Mariah Carey’s brother, five years after he accused her of defaming him in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey.
In the memoir, Carey described Morgan as a “sometimes drug dealing, been-in-the-system, drunk-ass brother” and called him her “ex-brother”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mariah Carey wins dismissal of brother’s defamation lawsuit over her memoir

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Vietnam veteran William Reaves executed by lethal injection despite letter from fellow veterans urging halt
Florida carried out its 18th execution of the year on Tuesday under Republican governor Ron DeSantis’s aggressive use of the death penalty in his final term.
William Reaves, 77, was pronounced dead at 6.12pm following a three-drug injection at Florida state prison near Starke. He was convicted of first-degree murder in the 1986 shooting death of Indian River county deputy Richard Raczkowski.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida kills 77-year-old man in state’s 18th execution of year

articles.author: Dani Anguiano
articles.description:
Toforest Johnson’s death penalty reduced to life in prison without parole over doubts about his conviction
Toforest Johnson, an Alabama death row inmate, will no longer face execution after the state’s Republican governor commuted his sentence amid increasing doubts about his conviction.
Kay Ivey, the Alabama governor, commuted Johnson’s sentence to life in prison without parole in the 1995 murder of William Hardy, a Jefferson county deputy sheriff. Johnson has long maintained he is innocent, and several former public officials, as well the local district attorney, have argued he should receive a new trial.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alabama governor commutes sentence of prisoner on death row

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome and Jon Henley in Paris
articles.description:
Government planning tougher security measures as France also says military forces will be deployed

Why are people protesting across Europe?

Italy’s government is sending 500 soldiers to Milan and vowed a “firm response from the state” after protests against the cost of living descended into clashes with police, vandalism and looting. Further demonstrations are planned on Saturday.
The government of the far-right prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, also announced new security measures, including an offence of violent participation in ⁠a demonstration, tougher penalties for ⁠rioters, and financial liability for ​parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Italy to deploy 500 troops to Milan after days of protests and looting

articles.author: Luke Harding
articles.description:
Advance warnings of missile attacks were seemingly suspended last week by the White House, but Ukraine’s president says: ‘Now it works’
The US has resumed sharing intelligence with Kyiv about Russian missile strikes, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday after a meeting with the US envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway.
He said Ukraine was again receiving advance warnings of ballistic missile attacks, which were seemingly suspended last week by the White House. “Now it works. It’s great,” he said, adding that the US move would save lives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine about Russian strikes, says Zelenskyy

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns
Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials said on Facebook.
The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Admission from James Orr to undercover reporter came three months before party was given £72m
A senior Reform UK official raised questions about whether major donations from billionaire backers Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo would be legal under the proposed new foreign donors cap three months before they gave £72m to the party.
James Orr, who was then Reform UK’s head of policy and a Cambridge professor, discussed potential difficulties around future donations from Harborne and Delo in undercover footage captured by the investigative reporting group Verbatim.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senior Reform official cast doubt over legality of huge donations

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
RAF Typhoon fighters to fly defensive missions over cities and infrastructure in extension of UK support for Riyadh
RAF Typhoon fighters are to be used in efforts to protect Saudi Arabia from attack by Yemen’s Houthis, flying protective missions over the country’s cities and critical infrastructure as western allies increase their intervention in the escalating conflict.
The operation – the most significant military mission signed off by Andy Burnham as prime minister – will involve RAF pilots attempting to shoot down Houthi missiles and drones, which attacked Saudi airports and oil facilities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to deploy fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Jackdaw gasfield announcement signals UK’s commitment to North Sea industry but undermines green credentials

What does the approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?

The Jackdaw gasfield will be given the go-ahead on Wednesday, signalling Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry and threatening to trigger a row with climate campaigners and Labour MPs.
Miatta Fahnbulleh and John Healey, the energy secretary and chancellor respectively, will make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning after more than a year of deliberations over whether doing so would violate the UK’s climate commitments.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham faces climate revolt after approval of North Sea gas drilling

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz
articles.description:
Woman says alleged assault at comedian’s London home was one of most painful experiences of her life
A woman has said she “couldn’t speak or breathe” when Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after picking her out from a crowd after one of his gigs, a court has heard.
She said the comedian looked “horrified” after the alleged attack so she assumed he would apologise but instead he told her: “Clear up the mess you’ve made.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand told woman to ‘clear up the mess you’ve made’ after alleged rape, court hears

articles.author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
articles.description:
Mounting anxiety as Russia’s war on Ukraine reaches Nato’s borders with targeting of vessels transporting agricultural cargo
Nato is deploying additional military assets to the Black Sea amid the recent deadly escalation of Russian attacks on merchant shipping, as five more vessels were attacked on Tuesday.
Russia’s military said it ⁠struck ​three cargo vessels in Ukraine’s ⁠port of Reni and two ⁠other cargo vessels en ​route ‌to ‌Odesa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nato increases Black Sea deployment amid escalating deadly Russian attacks

articles.author: Jakub Krupa (now) and Yohannes Lowe (earlier)
articles.description:
The Ukrainian leader says talks with US envoys covered security guarantees and he hopes to hear Russia’s response tomorrow
Nordic correspondent
As well as Steve Witkoff, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy will also meet the Norwegian prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre and the Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norway’s new King Haakon during his visit to Oslo.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine thankful that intelligence on missile strikes ‘works now’, says Zelenskyy – as it happened

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman, North of England Correspondent
articles.description:
Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023 after doctors put her symptoms down to Covid-19
A baby girl who died from meningitis may have been saved if doctors had tested her for the infection sooner, rather than putting her symptoms down to Covid, an inquest jury has found.
Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023, days after she was taken into the emergency department with a high temperature and vomiting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Baby who died from meningitis may have been saved if tested sooner, inquest finds

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity
Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.
With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mitchell Fairbarn found guilty of animal cruelty after prosecutors say he hurt and frightened the 27-year-old bird
A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel.
Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Bad decisions’: Man convicted for taking Peachy the flamingo from Las Vegas hotel

articles.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
articles.description:
Far-right presidential candidate’s TV debate swipe at rival backfires as people take to social media to parody it
To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election.
But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand has backfired.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Researchers say almost 90% of participants in unconditional basic income scheme in Peru adopted environmentally beneficial practices
A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study.
The analysis from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payments to communities that maintain globally important ecosystems.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Giving £2 a day to people in the Amazon helps protect rainforest, pilot project finds

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday
India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.
Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup, grumbling over mathematics homework and hanging out with friends at a tea stall.
That month, as the fever of student protests spread across the country, the 15-year-old watched on her phone as young people poured into Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in Delhi, demanding education reform. She went too. But an 11-second video clip from the protest site, in which she made crude and profane remarks about the prime minister, Narendra Modi, upended her life.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: She was harassed for crude remarks about Modi at a Cockroach protest. Now she can’t leave home

articles.author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
articles.description:
Critics said images of detained former leader were a stunt by the military to end country’s diplomatic isolation
Myanmar has delivered presents from Britain’s ​King Charles to Aung San Suu Kyi, releasing rare photos of the imprisoned former leader in what critics said was a stunt by the country’s military to end diplomatic isolation.
A presidential spokesperson said on social media that home ministry officials handed over two gardening books on soil, “along with one sealed envelope and a sealed diplomatic pouch”, from King Charles, who is known to have an interest in planting and the environment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Myanmar’s ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi seen in rare photos after receiving gift from King Charles

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.
Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Move comes after US photojournalist and group of European diplomats and Palestinians were assaulted in separate attacks
Israeli police have detained 10 people in a rare raid against settlers, after a weekend of extreme violence in the occupied West Bank including an attack on US photojournalist Heidi Levine, which she described as an “attempted lynching”.
She was knocked down, kicked and beaten by a group of masked Israeli men as she covered the olive harvest in a Palestinian village on Friday. The militants broke four vertebrae and a rib, ripped open her finger so it required surgery and left her with lacerations across her body.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli police detain 10 people in rare raid against West Bank settlers

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces 
At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.
The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors
A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history.
Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
At least 15 vessels struck in waterway in past 10 days, with rumours that they were carrying valuable goods
People have been scouring the strait of Hormuz for spilt cargo after Iran attacked at least 15 container ships passing through the crucial waterway in the past 10 days.
Some ships have been hit by drones, others by mines. On Sunday, a ship was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade launched from a small boat 75 miles (120km) north-east of the Saudi port of Jubail.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: People scour strait of Hormuz for spilt cargo after Iran attacks container ships

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi and agencies
articles.description:
Witness says drone struck twice at transport hub in al-Dibab, in one of deadliest single attacks of war
A drone strike near a market in southern Sudan on Sunday evening killed 80 people, mostly commuters catching rides home.
Ahmed Wadi, a witness, said the attack in the town of al-Dibab in West Kordofan state left “50 bodies who I helped bury, one of them my own brother Mohamed”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Drone attack near market kills 80 in Sudan

articles.author: Alice Nightingale-Smith and Nick Lee for MetDesk
articles.description:
Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece
In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.
Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand
Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.
China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhere
There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country.
Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three deaths from float crushes raise safety concerns over Japanese festivals

articles.author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
articles.description:
Expedition was drawn to Nikumaroro after spotting what was described as a metallic glint in waters off uninhabited island
A US expedition that voyaged to a remote Pacific island in the hope of solving the mystery of what happened to pioneering pilot Amelia Earhart has said an object they suspected to be her plane was a clump of washed-up trees.
“Unfortunately, we weren’t able to find that smoking gun,” said Steve Schultz of Purdue University, standing on the sand in front of a blue lagoon on the atoll of Nikumaroro, about halfway between Australia and Hawaii.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Amelia Earhart researchers leave remote atoll empty-handed after ‘plane debris’ found to be a clump of trees

articles.author: Rowena Mason, Lisa O’Carroll and Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package
No 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.
Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act” after France dropped its opposition to Britain joining the scheme.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Abhijeet Dipke was detained before planned anti-government demonstrations in Delhi
The leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and then later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital.
Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader arrested amid crackdown on protests

articles.author: Matt Andrews and Ed Walton for MetDesk
articles.description:
Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal
Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged.
After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority reported that 204 homes were damaged, and more than 650 people had been affected. More than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the popular hiking region. The floods come just two months after catastrophic flooding and landslides devastated parts of the country on the border with Tibet, leaving thousands dead or missing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flash floods destroy villages in central Nepal

articles.author: Oliver Holmes
articles.description:
Images from New Zealand aerial survey of Nikumaroro in 1938 offer new clues over aviator’s disappearance
A New Zealand museum has released nearly 50 photos from a 1938 aerial survey of the island where Amelia Earhart is believed to have crash-landed, offering amateur sleuths new evidence to scour for traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.
The black-and-white images were published by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand after renewed interest in one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century, spurred by a US expedition to the Pacific atoll of Nikumaroro in search of new clues.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Museum releases historical photos of island where Amelia Earhart may have crashed

articles.author: Dani Anguiano, Uwa Ede-Osifo, Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat and Maya Yang (earlier)
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

A new survey reveals a widening “empathy gap” between Republicans and white evangelicals and the rest of the American public.
On Tuesday, the nonpartisan Public Religion Research Institute released its annual American Values Survey. The survey found that white evangelical Protestants are the only religious group in which a majority does not agree that empathy is foundational moral value (42%). Instead, a majority (54%) say empathy can be dangerous when it leads people away from a society guided by God’s truth, PRRI said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he will have spent $400m to support Republicans in midterms – as it happened

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Anti-Defamation League post decries ‘shylock’ slur but does not explain that president used it at Kansas rally on Monday
The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) denounced the use of the term “shylock” as antisemitic on Tuesday, without explaining that the slur had been used a day earlier by Donald Trump in a speech in Kansas.
Trump used the slur during a Monday night rally in support of Republican senator Roger Marshall, who is locked in a closer-than-expected re-election fight against Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton. Marshall, a doctor, as been criticized for filing lawsuits against more than 700 patients with outstanding bills, leading to 18 of them being arrested.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ADL condemns Trump’s antisemitic slur but fails to mention him by name

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Billionaire ex-mayor of New York City is focusing funds on House races to help Democrats retake majority in midterms

US politics live – latest updates

The billionaire Michael Bloomberg will spend $80m to help Democratic candidates in the midterm elections, US media reported on Tuesday, a significant infusion of cash for a party that has recently struggled with fundraising as it seeks to win control of Congress.
The reported donations came as Donald Trump announced on Tuesday he intended to spend a total of $400m to aid Republican candidates, with $300m already disbursed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michael Bloomberg spends $80m on Democrats as Trump moves $400m to Republican candidates

articles.author: Ariana Baio
articles.description:
President makes suggestion while announcing new program to reward tipsters who submit fraud allegations
Donald Trump suggested on Tuesday that he would serve as “the arbitrator” of decisions in the justice department’s new anti-fraud program that awards compensation to those who submit tips resulting in conviction or significant federal enforcement.
While announcing the new program alongside JD Vance, the vice-president, who leads the White House’s taskforce to eliminate fraud, the president told reporters he had a solution for situations where multiple people submit a tip for the same alleged fraud.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump suggests he could be ‘arbitrator’ in DoJ anti-fraud whistleblower scheme

articles.author: Rachel Leingang in Topeka
articles.description:
Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1932 – does Adam Hamilton have the courage, brain and heart to cause an extraordinary upset?
Just two years after Donald Trump won Kansas by 16 points in his fight to regain the White House, Republicans in the state are scrambling to retain their dominance. The battle for one of its two seats in the US Senate is too close to call, setting the stage for a potentially extraordinary upset.
Some recent polls even put Democrat Adam Hamilton on course for a historic victory. Kansans have not sent a representative of the party to the US Senate since 1932.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kansas Democrat’s pitch to voters amid historic Senate bid: ‘I’m gonna just fight like hell’

articles.author: Rebecca Solnit
articles.description:
The midterms will be a referendum on the GOP’s alignment with tech overlords over the public they’re meant to serve
Welcome back to How We Win, a Guardian opinion series with leading thinkers, offering bold ideas for America’s political future. Last week, Robert Reich highlighted the link between corruption and affordability. Today’s edition was written by Guardian US columnist Rebecca Solnit. Sign up for future editions here.
“The world should accept some bad things happening,” Sam Altman, the head of OpenAI, said recently, “for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.” Like so many things tech oligarchs say, it’s incoherent, since Altman would like to deny the world and the people in it the agency to decide whether or not we should accept his bad things. Surveys show that most Americans would like to pause AI; opposition to AI datacenters is a factor in many races in the midterm elections. People are outraged and anxious about what tech hath wrought, mad enough to fight back in what is coming to seem like a human v machine battle.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Americans, this is your chance to slap down the tech broligarchs

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
The administration seems intent on stripping the congresswoman of her US citizenship and deporting her. It’s a terrible abuse of power
What do you think it is about Ilhan Omar, exactly, that seems to get under Donald Trump’s tangerine-tinted skin? The president has claimed he has a problem with the progressive Democratic congresswoman because she is “unpatriotic” to the US and “disrespectful … to Israel”. However, the extent of his animus towards Omar, the first Somali American in Congress, suggests there’s more to it. Trump has insisted he is “the least racist person there is anywhere in the world”, so I’m sure it has nothing to do with the fact that she’s brown and Muslim. Truly, it’s a mystery.
Whatever the reason, Trump’s not a fan. The president has plenty of enemies, but few have been attacked as ferociously and consistently over the years as Omar. He’s called her “garbage”, among other nasty names, suggested (without evidence) that she married her brother, and said she “should be thrown the hell out of our country”. His supporters have echoed his calls to deport Omar, who fled war-torn Somalia as a child and became a naturalised US citizen at 17.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s obsession with Ilhan Omar has reached a dangerous new level | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Kenneth Roth
articles.description:
Here’s what we need to do to stand up for international law
Many applauded when Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel peace prize. The South African human rights lawyer had chaired the UN commission of inquiry that found Israel to have committed genocide in Gaza and served for five years as a judge on the international criminal court (ICC).
Donald Trump responded a few hours later by imposing sanctions on the ICC. He chose a moment for celebrating the rule of law to try to undermine it.
Kenneth Roth is a Guardian US columnist, a senior fellow at Yale University and a former executive director of Human Rights Watch. He is the author of Righting Wrongs: Three Decades on the Front Lines Battling Abusive Governments
 Continue reading...
articles.title: We can stop Trump’s assault on the international criminal court | Kenneth Roth

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
Russia wants America and China to decide Ukraine’s future without Kyiv. Europe must challenge this dangerous return to diplomacy of the strong for the strong
Does Vladimir Putin know exactly how to play Donald Trump? The history of chummy phone calls, high-profile meetings and attempts to bring Russia in from the cold certainly suggests that Moscow’s thuggish ruler has a hold on this American president. If Mr Trump agrees to negotiate Ukraine’s future with Mr Putin and China’s Xi Jinping without Ukraine at the table, he will have handed the Russian leader a victory before talks begin. The message will be that strongmen are ruling the world and determining the fate of weaker nations.
Ukraine has the right to determine its future. That right cannot be waved away by a self-serving Russian proposal, however much it indulges Mr Trump’s belief that world affairs should be settled by powerful men. The scales are falling from European eyes. Trumpian America is raising doubts about whether it will help deter aggression or even honour its Nato commitments. If Washington now rewards Moscow and pressures Ukraine to accept a raw deal, it would be a betrayal. European governments would wonder where America might be in the future when their own security is threatened.
Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on Trump and Putin: Ukraine’s future is not theirs to bargain away | Editorial

articles.author: Melody Schreiber
articles.description:
Opposition to US-led quarantine center in Kenya follows sweeping funding cuts and withdrawal from WHO
An eighth person in Kenya has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the country’s first-ever cluster of cases of the virus, as the second-largest outbreak in history has killed more than 4,300 and sickened more than 9,000 people in the region.
It highlights the diminished role the US has played in the worsening Ebola outbreak by building a controversial quarantine center in Kenya, pulling back health support globally, and banning travelers from certain countries. All of this has also reduced the ability to identify and respond to the outbreak and exacerbated mistrust.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ebola cases in Kenya highlight US failures amid Trump cuts to key services

articles.author: Michael Sainato in Fort Edward, New York
articles.description:
Anthony Constantino wants to fill Elise Stefanik’s seat in New York. But his lead in the formerly Trump-loving district is narrowing
The boss of a New York-based sticker company, whose staunch support for Donald Trump prompted him to record a Maga-themed rap album and call for an extension of Mount Rushmore to add the president’s face, is running for Congress.
Anthony Constantino, who began a brief pro boxing career at age 40, is the Republican candidate for GOP congresswoman Elise Stefanik’s seat in New York’s 21st district.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sticker tycoon. Trump cheerleader. Rapper. Congressman?

articles.author: Sam Levine in New York
articles.description:
From the attorney general stumping for Republican candidates to federal agents raiding the home of a Democratic congresswoman up for re-election, the department is violating longstanding norms
Donald Trump’s justice department has aggressively inserted itself into the midterm elections in the contest’s final weeks, shattering the department’s longstanding practice of political neutrality and leaving little doubt about the department’s willingness to help should the president attempt to subvert elections where his party is forecasted to lose seats and ultimately control of Congress.
In the last few weeks, federal agents have raided the home of a Democratic congresswoman up for re-election. It has touted criminal charges and arrests of non-citizens charged with voter fraud. The attorney general has hit the campaign trail to stump for Republican candidates. And the department gave California election officials 48 hours to investigate the citizenship of 20,000 people, and then sued the state when it refused to comply. The FBI also recently published a video criticizing Michigan senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and other Democrats, drawing an immediate rebuke from one watchdog, who said the video “has no place in a democratic society”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Trump’s justice department is shattering practice of political neutrality as midterms loom

articles.description:
Protesters held rallies across the US as part of the 'No Kings' movement, voicing opposition to the Trump administration and calling for early voting ahead of November's midterm elections. The rallies coincide with heightened legal battles surrounding voting rules, including a recent federal lawsuit filed against California regarding mail-in ballots and warnings from the justice department concerning ballot processing. Current opinion polls suggest Democrats will win the House of Representatives in the upcoming midterms, while the Senate remains too close to call
 Continue reading...
articles.title: 'No Kings' protesters rally across the US – video

articles.author: J Oliver Conroy
articles.description:
The Republican state attorney general appears uniquely ill-chosen as a candidate – but he is a political survivor who could yet frustrate Democratic dreams
Depending how you look at the situation, it is either predictable that Ken Paxton, Texas’s attorney general and Republican candidate for US Senate, is struggling in the polls – or impressive that he is not doing worse. Beloved by hardcore Maga voters and regarded with skepticism by the broader voting public, Paxton is also puzzlingly bland. Recently, Donald Trump told a crowd of supporters that the 63-year-old Paxton “may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen”. The president was endorsing him.
Yet it is Paxton’s ability to attract – and somehow scrape through – scandal that makes him a less charismatic, perhaps, but still kindred spirit of “Teflon Don”: nothing sticks. He has survived state prosecution (on securities-related charges that he settled without admitting guilt), impeachment by the Republican-led Texas legislature (on abuse-of-office charges of which he was later acquitted), and so many controversies that it can be difficult to pin down the most outrageous.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Getaway cars, affairs, Dubai fugitives: Trump’s pick Ken Paxton brings baggage to Senate race in Texas

articles.description:
Katie Zacharia, the new White House press secretary, has been fired from her role after just five days. Moments before the firing, Donald Trump told reporters he would suggest Zacharia to 'reconsider' the job, following days of intense media scrutiny around her legal credentials

Katie Zacharia fired after five days as White House press secretary

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he will advise Katie Zacharia to reconsider shortly before she was fired - video

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Arwa Mahdawi , produced by Nada Smiljanic and Danielle Stephens
articles.description:
The US vice-president is following the Donald Trump playbook, attacking the Democrats, attempting to make jokes and even swearing more. Jonathan Freedland talks to Arwa Mahdawi about why Vance is making such an effort to court voters
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is JD Vance campaigning for the midterms – or 2028? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Oliver Laughland, Tom Silverstone, Steve Glew, Ivan Kuraev and Katie Lamborn
articles.description:
As the midterm elections loom, Oliver Laughland and Tom Silverstone travel to rural West Virginia, a Republican party stronghold, to explore how soaring gas prices, war in the Middle East and datacenter expansion are affecting Donald Trump's popularity among his base. Although the state remains staunchly Republican, there are signs of a new politics emerging – and local Democrats are looking to capitalize on it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why one of the US's reddest counties is losing faith in Trump – video

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Exclusive: East Sussex MP Helena Dollimore says ‘shambolic’ museum phone line has made her constituents lose out to ‘queue jumpers’
Hastings residents have missed out on tickets for the Bayeux tapestry after being put on hold for hours by a “glitchy and shambolic” phone system, their MP has said.
People from “1066 Country” were promised a chance to buy before a sales line opened to the public on Wednesday. But Helena Dollimore, the MP for Hastings and Rye, said it has been almost impossible for her constituents to get through to the British Museum.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Residents of ‘1066 Country’ lose battle for Bayeux tapestry tickets

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
During a summer fire that destroyed homes in Stourbridge, low pressure meant filling a water carrier took 40 minutes
Concerns have been raised about how drought affects the UK’s ability to cope with wildfires after MPs were told firefighters struggled for water supplies during this year’s record summer.
The government has been urged to set out water companies’ statutory responsibilities during major fire incidents to improve the country’s preparedness for the years ahead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Firefighters voice growing concerns over water supplies to tackle UK wildfires

articles.author: Richard Adams Education editor
articles.description:
Government expected to accept recommendations of review, which found three in five Jewish students had experienced prejudice
Schools and colleges in England will be expected to take a tougher stance against antisemitism after a report found that three out of five Jewish students said they had been affected.
Sir David Bell, the former chief inspector of Ofsted who was commissioned by the government to lead the independent review, said he found many cases of antisemitism going unreported or unchallenged by students and teachers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Schools in England must recognise antisemitism as distinct category of harm, report says

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Decision has implications for household energy bills, the UK economy and the climate crisis

Andy Burnham faces climate revolt after approval of North Sea gas drilling


About four years and six energy secretaries after it was given the green light, the Jackdaw gasfield is to be given consent on Wednesday to begin production 150 miles east of Aberdeen.
So what will this long-awaited decision mean for the Labour party, household bills, the economy and the climate crisis?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What does the UK’s approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Admission from James Orr to undercover reporter came three months before party was given £72m
A senior Reform UK official raised questions about whether major donations from billionaire backers Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo would be legal under the proposed new foreign donors cap three months before they gave £72m to the party.
James Orr, who was then Reform UK’s head of policy and a Cambridge professor, discussed potential difficulties around future donations from Harborne and Delo in undercover footage captured by the investigative reporting group Verbatim.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senior Reform official cast doubt over legality of huge donations

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
RAF Typhoon fighters to fly defensive missions over cities and infrastructure in extension of UK support for Riyadh
RAF Typhoon fighters are to be used in efforts to protect Saudi Arabia from attack by Yemen’s Houthis, flying protective missions over the country’s cities and critical infrastructure as western allies increase their intervention in the escalating conflict.
The operation – the most significant military mission signed off by Andy Burnham as prime minister – will involve RAF pilots attempting to shoot down Houthi missiles and drones, which attacked Saudi airports and oil facilities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to deploy fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Jackdaw gasfield announcement signals UK’s commitment to North Sea industry but undermines green credentials

What does the approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?

The Jackdaw gasfield will be given the go-ahead on Wednesday, signalling Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry and threatening to trigger a row with climate campaigners and Labour MPs.
Miatta Fahnbulleh and John Healey, the energy secretary and chancellor respectively, will make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning after more than a year of deliberations over whether doing so would violate the UK’s climate commitments.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham faces climate revolt after approval of North Sea gas drilling

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz
articles.description:
Woman says alleged assault at comedian’s London home was one of most painful experiences of her life
A woman has said she “couldn’t speak or breathe” when Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after picking her out from a crowd after one of his gigs, a court has heard.
She said the comedian looked “horrified” after the alleged attack so she assumed he would apologise but instead he told her: “Clear up the mess you’ve made.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand told woman to ‘clear up the mess you’ve made’ after alleged rape, court hears

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Counter-terrorism police say 24 and 25-year-old from central London detained under 2023 National Security Act
Counter-terrorism police have re-arrested two men from central London accused of helping Iranian intelligence as part of the investigation into events at RAF Fairford last month.
A 24-year-old UK national and a 25-year-old UK/Iranian national, both from Westminster, were detained on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service in breach of the 2023 National Security Act, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two men re-arrested on suspicion of aiding Iran over RAF Fairford incident

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman, North of England Correspondent
articles.description:
Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023 after doctors put her symptoms down to Covid-19
A baby girl who died from meningitis may have been saved if doctors had tested her for the infection sooner, rather than putting her symptoms down to Covid, an inquest jury has found.
Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023, days after she was taken into the emergency department with a high temperature and vomiting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Baby who died from meningitis may have been saved if tested sooner, inquest finds

articles.author: Ben Quinn
articles.description:
Jurors in harassment trial told reporters who had written about far-right activist feared ‘vigilante attack’
Tommy Robinson told the Daily Mail’s editor he would make the paper’s journalists and their families “famous”, the harassment trial of the far-right activist has been told.
The threat was made in a voicemail message left on the phone of Ted Verity as Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, allegedly waged a campaign of harassment against journalists from the newspaper.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I’ll make you famous’: court hears recording of Tommy Robinson threat to Daily Mail editor

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Latest report paints a painful picture of the care sector during the pandemic. But timid recommendations and a lack of accountability threaten to undermine it
Of all 10 reports due to be published by the long-running Covid-19 inquiry, this week’s findings on adult social care were especially anticipated.
The impact of Covid-19 on the care sector was calamitous: tens of thousands of people died, staff were forced to wear bin bags due to a lack of protective clothing and relatives were banned from seeing their loved ones in their dying days.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Superficial damp squib’: Covid inquiry recommendations fail to impress bereaved families

articles.author: Aisha Down
articles.description:
Our dependence on internet services of a few key tech companies leaves us vulnerable to cloud failures, bugs and more, experts say
It happened again. A power outage hit a datacentre in London, and things cascaded from there: multiple banking services faltered, court hearings were put on hold and patients reported temporary glitches on the NHS app.
The datacentre in question was in Google’s europe-west2-b zone, one of more than a dozen “zones” that the US search giant maintains in Europe to service its clients.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Too big to not fail’: Google outage exposes UK reliance on a handful of cloud providers

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
The prime minister endorses report that says the adult social care sector has been under-recognised
Badenoch says Britain needs tax cuts.
We need to get out of the way of job creators who make our country richer. We need to encourage risk taking, wealth creation, enterprise.
Britain’s tax burden has never been higher. You are taxed on the heating in your home. You’re taxed at the petrol pump filling up your car. You’re taxed when you insure that car. You’re taxed if you take the family away on holiday. You’re taxed if you stay in the UK thanks to Andy Burnham’s tourist tax. You’re taxed to buy a home, taxed to live in a home, taxed to pass on your home. This is clearly not working. Britain does not feel better off.
Andy Burnham wrote in The Times yesterday about the moral outrage of the current benefit system. But as far as I could work out, his answer is to spend even more on benefits.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Covid inquiry report shows why culture of care workers being undervalued must end, says Andy Burnham – as it happened

articles.author: Matthew Weaver
articles.description:
Lawyers tell inquiry that patients’ lives are at stake through improper use of Oxevision system for most vulnerable
Families bereaved by the misuse of an “intrusive” camera monitoring system for vulnerable patients used in half of England’s mental health wards have called for it to be banned to help prevent more avoidable deaths.
Lawyers for the families said “patients’ lives are at stake” by the continuing use of Oxevision, the Lampard inquiry into mental health deaths in Essex heard on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ban ‘intrusive’ cameras in England’s mental health wards, say bereaved families

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
City’s Beatles Story museum to move to 100,000 sq ft new home and official ownership, along with Yellow Submarine makeover of Liverpool’s second-tallest building
Liverpool is to unveil a new 100,000 sq ft visitor attraction about the Beatles, in plans hailed as “extraordinary” by Paul McCartney, and by Andy Burnham as having “the kind of ambition I want to see more of across Britain”.
Opening in 2028, the project is a huge upgrade for the Beatles Story, a museum which opened in Liverpool’s Royal Albert Dock in 1990. Ownership will now pass to the Beatles company Apple Corps, making the Beatles Story the band’s first official fan experience in their home city.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Vast Beatles museum, hailed as ‘extraordinary’ by Paul McCartney, to open in Liverpool in 2028

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Flutter says one in 10 UK and Ireland workers at risk of redundancy because of a ‘material increase in betting and gaming duties’
The gambling company behind Paddy Power and Sky Bet has announced up to 1,400 job cuts, blaming tax rises imposed by Rachel Reeves.
Flutter Entertainment revealed plans on Tuesday to restructure its UK and Ireland division, affecting staff in Leeds, Dublin and Sunderland. Redundancies are also expected to hit offices in Porto in Portugal and Cluj-Napoca in Romania.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Paddy Power owner blames tax rises for plan to shed up to 1,400 jobs

articles.description:
Amateur wildlife photographer Rhys Morgan has caught extraordinary footage of one of the largest whale species on Earth. 

While sailing off the Pembrokeshire coast in Wales, Morgan and his friends spotted the blowholes of a fin whale in the distance, recognisable by the hooked fin near its tail, a dark grey upper body, white belly, and an asymmetrical jaw that is dark on the left and white on the right.

People who have enjoyed the video online are trying to raise awareness of fin whales being hunted in Iceland and calling on government ministers to take action
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Whale in Wales: amateur photographer captures stunning footage - video

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Inquiry chair says failure to advise care homes to isolate people discharged from hospital was ‘significant oversight’
Government failures caused Covid-19 to spread “like wildfire” among vulnerable and elderly people, and Matt Hancock’s “protective ring” around care homes did not exist, a public inquiry has found.
Heather Hallett, who is leading the Covid-19 inquiry, said the care sector was an “afterthought” and rejected the former health secretary’s long-held claim that he threw a “protective ring” around care homes from the start of the pandemic, saying it was “unfounded” and the “opposite was true”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government failures led to Covid spreading ‘like wildfire’ in care homes, inquiry finds

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Stricken UK water supplier lines up John Hutton as independent chair designate if takeover goes ahead
The group of Thames Water creditors pursuing a £10bn rescue deal for Britain’s largest water supplier has lined up a former senior Labour minister to chair the company, as it tries to win over the government.
The creditor consortium, called London & Valley Water, said on Tuesday that Lord John Hutton had been selected as independent chair designate of the Thames Water board, if the consortium’s deal is approved.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thames Water creditors secure former Labour minister to drive rescue deal

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff and Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Services restored for most users, but power fault stalled hearings and left Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC customers unable to pay or move money
An outage at Google’s cloud services in the UK has caused widespread disruption, hitting courts and leaving millions of customers unable to access or send cash at banks including Lloyds, HSBC and Revolut.
Google blamed a “power event” for the failure at its London-based Cloud computing operations on Tuesday, which affected its “europe-west2-b zone”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Google cloud failure hits millions as UK courts and banks knocked offline

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Adrian Ramsay calls conference motion a distraction and says councillors should maintain coalitions where possible
Adrian Ramsay, the former co-leader of the Greens, has urged his party’s councillors to reject the newly adopted “Zionism is racism” motion if it will help them stay in power in local government, in a fresh sign of internal dissent over the policy.
Ramsay, one of the Greens’ five MPs, said he was pleased that a number of Green council groups had already condemned the policy, which was adopted at the party’s conference and also calls for a single Palestinian state in place of Israel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-Greens co-leader urges council groups to reject Zionism policy

articles.author: Phillip Inman Senior economics writer and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Latest ONS data presents mixed picture amid slump in job vacancies and analysts warning labour market is ‘running on idle’

Healey to reject calls to raise CGT in budget

Unemployment in the UK has fallen unexpectedly in the final snapshot of the jobs market before John Healey’s first budget next week.
The jobless rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, from 4.9%, according to the Office for National Statistics. City economists had forecast a rise to 5%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Surprise drop in UK unemployment to 4.7% as John Healey’s first budget looms

articles.author: Chris Wiegand Stage editor
articles.description:
Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie will explore how the musician ‘practised a form of artistic reincarnation’, says choreographer Marcos Morau
‘Let’s dance,” sang David Bowie in 1983, commanding: “Put on your red shoes and dance the blues.” That call is to be answered – with footwear TBC – by an international dance production featuring new choral arrangements of songs from throughout his career.
Subject to Change: A Dance for David Bowie will be staged at Sadler’s Wells in London in autumn 2028 after a world premiere in Luxembourg. It will visit Tokyo in 2029. The show will explore how Bowie “practised a form of artistic reincarnation” according to Spanish choreographer Marcos Morau who is taking inspiration from the superstar’s transformations into personas such as Aladdin Sane and the Thin White Duke.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Getting Ziggy with it: David Bowie’s alter egos inspire dance show that will transform his songs

articles.author: Sarah Marsh Consumer affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Some users claim online marketplace’s automated systems stack odds against them when sales go wrong
After Catherine Warrilow sold a Zara necklace for £6 on Vinted, she packed it up and posted it off, just as she had done with many things before. Only this time the buyer claimed the parcel arrived empty.
Warrilow, 47, from Oxford, provided Vinted with photos and videos of the package, including date-stamped Ring doorbell footage of her leaving the house to post it. But she says the resale platform refunded the buyer and left her out of pocket.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No real sense of appeal’: Vinted sellers complain of unfair account ‘bans’

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Around one in eight 16- to 24-year-olds are ‘Neet’ – and Alan Milburn is hinting that the overhaul of their support may be controversial
With nearly 1 million young people not in education, employment or training (a cohort known as “Neets”), the government and its advisers have signalled that welfare benefits may be cut to fund more job support for them. What may change and who will be affected?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Who exactly will be affected by the UK review of benefits for young people?

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Rise in economic hardship and changes in attitudes towards migration could explain drop in support, experts say
Public support for the NHS’s founding principles – that it is free to use, available to everyone and tax-funded – has fallen over the last five years, research has shown.
Backing for all three pillars dropped between 2021 and 2025 across the UK population, except for a small rise in millennials’ support for the NHS being funded from taxation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Public support for founding principles of NHS is falling across UK population

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Zoe Williams and Haroon Siddique; produced by Ruth Abrahams, Eleanor Biggs and Rudi Zygadlo
articles.description:
The bestselling author says her books will no longer be supplied to UK bookshops over fears of prosecution. Zoe Williams and Haroon Siddique report
For now there might be a copy or two of Intermezzo left kicking around in your local bookshop – snap it up if you haven’t already, because soon that will be it.
Last year, Sally Rooney said she would be using her royalties to support Palestine Action, a group that is proscribed as a terrorist organisation under UK law. articles.description:
People share their opinions of Andy Burnham's crackdown on 'headphone dodgers' who play loud music on public transport. The prime minister unveiled a campaign against nuisance behaviour on Monday, alongside guidance allowing local transport authorities to levy fines of up to £100 for non-compliance

Andy Burnham launches campaign against ‘headphone dodgers’ on public transport

 Continue reading...
articles.title: British people react to Burnham's campaign against ‘headphone dodgers’ on public transport – video

Undercover footage seen by the Guardian shows a close aide to Nigel Farage admitting the Reform leader did not follow the party's press office advice when he said his £5m gift from the crypto-billionaire Christopher Harborne was a thankyou for Brexit. The footage raises fresh questions about the party leader’s statements that the gift was solely for security purposes. Dan Jukes also tells the undercover reporter from Verbatim, who was posing as a donor, that the public expects Farage to make money from politics, saying 'no one's voting for him to be the pope'. Farage is awaiting the outcome of a parliamentary watchdog investigation into whether or not the £5m from the crypto-billionaire Christopher Harborne, first revealed by the Guardian, should have been declared under parliamentary rules

articles.title: Dan Jukes reveals Nigel Farage did not take press office line on £5m gift - video

articles.description:
Neso control room staff accused senior executives of covering up extent of blackout risks during June heatwave
Independent investigators have found significant and concerning “cultural issues” at Great Britain’s grid operator after control room staff accused senior executives of covering up the extent of blackout risks in the UK during the June heatwave.
An external legal firm tasked with investigating a series of whistleblower allegations against the National Energy System Operator (Neso) raised concerns over how high levels stress among control room engineers was handled by the company.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Concerning issues’ found at GB power grid by inquiry into cover-up claims

articles.author: Kevin Rawlinson
articles.description:
Singer ‘mortified’ about wearing diamonds from Argyle mine at centre of environmental concerns about Indigenous land
The singer Ellie Goulding has admitted her error at having promoted diamonds at the centre of environmental concerns about Indigenous land in Australia, despite having spent years campaigning on environmental issues – including the effects of mining on ancestral lands.
She appeared at a event in London earlier this month for the jewellery brand Boodles, modelling some of its newly acquired pink diamonds, some of which came from a controversial mine in Western Australia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ellie Goulding admits error over promoting diamonds from controversial Australian mine
